title: Jira Pricing 2026 for Project Tracking and Automation
summary: Atlassian Jira pricing has four cloud plans from Free to Enterprise. See the cost of each to decide which fits your team's needs.
body_markdown:
## Automating cross-tool Jira work with Activepieces


If the limit you would hit first is Jira's automation allowance, or the job spans several tools, Activepieces, an MIT-licensed automation tool with 750 integrations that you can self-host, runs that work outside Jira. It doesn't change what you pay per seat.


That distinction matters because the two costs are separate. Jira's built-in automation counts runs against your plan, so a busy team can hit the cap long before it hits a user limit.


Activepieces has a Jira connector and meters by the run: its published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module.


Those runs don't draw on Jira's allowance, so breaking a brittle workaround into ten small steps costs the same as the two-step version.


The Free plan's 1,000 credits a month, with unlimited flows, cover 1,000 runs of that ten-step flow, and you still pay Jira for every person who logs in, which means team costs are per-headcount.


In the workflow below, a new ticket arrives in HubSpot, the customer-relationship tool a support team might log requests in. HubSpot and Slack are two of Activepieces' 750 integrations, roughly 60% of which are community-contributed, so a job like this needs no custom connector.


After two AI steps rewrite and categorize the ticket, a router, which is a fork that sends each ticket down one path depending on its content, posts a message to the right Slack channel, which means each ticket is standardized and properly categorized before reaching the right team.


The panel on the right shows the trigger waiting for a new ticket, with test mode on and a publish button ready.


Nothing in that flow lives inside Jira, which is the point. Swap the first step for a Jira trigger and the same pattern covers an issue created in Jira that needs to reach a chat channel, a customer record, or a spreadsheet.


### When it fits and when it does not


It fits when the work crosses tool boundaries, or when automation runs are the first Jira limit you'd hit. It also suits a team that has someone able to host and maintain a server.


That upkeep is a real cost, and doing nothing about it means the server falls behind on updates.


It doesn't fit if your pressure is on users, storage, or support. Jira's 10-user Free cap, the 2 GB of Free storage and the business-hours support on Standard all sit on Atlassian's side of the line, and 1 credit per run changes none of them.


If those are your first limits, the Jira tier is still the decision.


As of 20 November 2026, the source for what the hosted version costs is[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/jira-pricing-in-2026-and-how-to-work-out-your-bill) 's own pricing page, not this article, and its plans and limits can change.
